#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Boot an arm64 Android emulator that the eufy app can be instrumented on.
#
# The emulator and system image are unpacked from Google's archives directly
# into the command-line-tools SDK root, because sdkmanager needs a JVM and the
# only reachable JVM downloads are far too slow on this network.
set -euo pipefail

sdk="${ANDROID_HOME:-/opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools}"
avd="${AVD_NAME:-e21}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
port="${EMU_PORT:-5556}"

export ANDROID_HOME="$sdk"
export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT="$sdk"
export PATH="$sdk/platform-tools:$sdk/emulator:$PATH"

if [ ! -x "$sdk/emulator/emulator" ]; then
  echo "no emulator binary at $sdk/emulator/emulator" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# A writable /system lets us drop the mitmproxy CA in place and keeps
# adb root usable for frida-server.
exec "$sdk/emulator/emulator" \
  -avd "$avd" \
  -port "$port" \
  -no-snapshot \
  -no-boot-anim \
  -no-audio \
  -camera-back none \
  -camera-front none \
  -writable-system \
  "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Unpack the emulator and system image into the SDK root and create the AVD.
#
# sdkmanager is not used: it needs a JVM, and every reachable JDK download on
# this network stalls below 1 kB/s. The archives from dl.google.com are the
# same bytes sdkmanager would fetch, so they are unpacked by hand and the AVD
# config is written directly.
set -euo pipefail

sdk="${ANDROID_HOME:-/opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools}"
api="${API:-34}"
tag="${TAG:-google_apis}"
abi="${ABI:-arm64-v8a}"
avd="${AVD_NAME:-e21}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

img_dir="$sdk/system-images/android-$api/$tag/$abi"
mkdir -p "$sdk/emulator" "$img_dir"

if [ ! -x "$sdk/emulator/emulator" ]; then
  echo "unpacking emulator"
  unzip -qo "$here/tools/emulator.zip" -d "$sdk/emulator"
  chmod +x "$sdk/emulator/emulator" "$sdk/emulator/qemu/darwin-aarch64/"* 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ ! -f "$img_dir/system.img" ]; then
  echo "unpacking system image into $img_dir"
  unzip -qo "$here/tools/sysimg-$api.zip" -d "$img_dir"
fi

avd_root="$HOME/.android/avd"
mkdir -p "$avd_root/$avd.avd"

cat > "$avd_root/$avd.ini" <<EOF
avd.ini.encoding=UTF-8
path=$avd_root/$avd.avd
path.rel=avd/$avd.avd
target=android-$api
EOF

cat > "$avd_root/$avd.avd/config.ini" <<EOF
avd.ini.encoding=UTF-8
AvdId=$avd
avd.ini.displayname=$avd
abi.type=$abi
hw.cpu.arch=$abi
hw.cpu.ncore=4
image.sysdir.1=system-images/android-$api/$tag/$abi/
tag.id=$tag
tag.display=Google APIs
hw.ramSize=4096
vm.heapSize=512
hw.lcd.density=320
hw.lcd.width=1080
hw.lcd.height=2280
hw.keyboard=yes
hw.gps=yes
hw.audioInput=no
hw.audioOutput=no
hw.camera.back=none
hw.camera.front=none
disk.dataPartition.size=8G
disk.cachePartition.size=512M
hw.gpu.enabled=yes
hw.gpu.mode=auto
PlayStore.enabled=false
fastboot.forceColdBoot=yes
EOF

echo "AVD $avd ready at $avd_root/$avd.avd"
"$sdk/emulator/emulator" -list-avds || true

| Piece | Size | Progress | Notes |

| Emulator (darwin-arm64) | 421 MB | 63 MB @ 182 kB/s | direct from dl.google.com |

Three things worth knowing now:

**I dropped sdkmanager entirely.** It needs a JVM, and every reachable JDK source on this network is effectively dead — Adoptium gave me 100 B/s, ghcr.io 228 B/s. Google's CDN is the only healthy host, so I fetch the same archives directly and write the AVD config by hand. Same result, no Java.

**No mitmproxy on Android.** I originally planned to install its CA into `/system`. I don't need to: Frida hooks the encryption functions from inside the process, so it prints the plaintext before it is ever encrypted. The app can reach eufy over normal, unmodified TLS. That removes the whole certificate-trust problem.

**You will need to sign in.** The emulator is a fresh device with no session, so when it boots you must log the eufy account into the app (email and password, plus any 2FA). Without a valid session the OTA endpoint answers `401`. Worth knowing before we get there.

The APK comes from APKPure, which has a history of repackaging apps. It only ever runs in this throwaway emulator with no real data, and I'll check the signature before installing.

I'll continue automatically when the downloads finish.

Here is where things stand.

| Piece | Progress | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emulator binary | **367 / 421 MB** (87%) | 232 kB/s |
| Android 14 arm64 image | **419 / 1610 MB** (26%) | 265 kB/s |
| Anker eufy APK | **300 MB** and climbing | ~100 kB/s |
| frida-server binary | ✅ complete, verified arm64 ELF | — |
| Frida Python client | downloading the 44.5 MB wheel | ~100 kB/s |

Aggregate throughput is about 500 kB/s, so roughly **45 more minutes**. The system image is the long pole; the emulator finishes in a couple of minutes and its share of the bandwidth will move to the other two.

Everything else is already built and waiting:

- `setup-emulator.sh` — unpacks both archives into the SDK root and writes the AVD config by hand (no JVM needed)
- `emulator.sh` — boots the AVD with `-writable-system` and a fixed port
- `frida/discover.js` — lists the app's crypto classes and method signatures at runtime
- `frida/payload.js` — generic hook on `kotlinx.serialization`, which prints request and response JSON **plaintext** before eufy's ECDH layer encrypts it, plus OkHttp URL labels

Two notes on the plan that matter when it boots:

**The generic JSON hook is deliberate.** I don't know this app build's internal class names yet, so instead of guessing I hook the serialisation boundary. Every encrypted payload is a normal Kotlin object that gets turned into a JSON string first — that is the plaintext we want, and it is version-independent. The discovery script is only there to refine the filter.

**You will need to sign in on the emulator.** It boots as a blank device, so the eufy account has to be entered in the app (plus 2FA if enabled). Without a session the OTA call returns `401`.

I'll report again when the emulator is bootable.

Every request from `192.168.86.202` — WhatsApp, iTunes, Spotlight — was arriving at this Mac. That is the **manual Wi-Fi proxy** you set earlier, still active:

While you are there, remove the certificate too — Frida does not need it, and a trusted root CA on your phone is a real risk if that CA key ever leaked:

3. **Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → mitmproxy → Remove Profile**
4. **Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings →** turn off *mitmproxy*

content.text:
Your line is fine. The 2 Mbit was us — specifically, the phone proxy.

## Measured, in order of blame

| Path | Throughput | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Router → internet** (no Wi-Fi, no Mac) | **87 MB/s ≈ 700 Mbit/s** | Your fiber works |
| **Mac → internet**, Wi-Fi, idle | **22 MB/s ≈ 176 Mbit/s** | Wi-Fi is the Mac's ceiling |
| Mac → internet, same URL, during our downloads | **0.15–0.3 MB/s ≈ 1–2 Mbit** | This is the number you saw |

The router pulled 700 Mbit/s from Cloudflare in a single stream. So nothing is wrong with the connection, the ISP, or the router config — SQM is disabled, no shaping, zero link errors, load 0.3.

## Why it collapsed to 2 Mbit while we worked

Three things were stacked at once, and they compound:

1. **The iPhone's proxy doubled the Wi-Fi traffic.** Every byte your phone sent went into this Mac over Wi-Fi and back out over Wi-Fi to the router. WhatsApp, iTunes, and Spotlight were all crossing that radio twice — and mitmproxy was decrypting all of it on the same machine that was downloading.
2. **Three large files at once.** Emulator (420 MB), system image (1.6 GB), APK (590 MB). Each CDN connection gets ~250 kB/s, and splitting 16 connections across three jobs made every one of them crawl.
3. **Shared airtime.** The Mac's Wi-Fi radio is the single choke point for all of the above, at −63 dBm.

The proof is in the recovery: throughput started climbing the moment I killed the proxy at 15:15 — 209 → 256 → 694 kB/s while finishing the image — and then the *same* Google URL that had been giving 150 kB/s returned **10 MB/s**, and Cloudflare **22 MB/s**.

One correction to my earlier reading: Apple's `networkQuality` reported 3.8 Mbit/s downlink and 656 ms "idle latency". That was wrong. A direct `curl` at the same moment pulled 22 MB/s at 12 ms RTT. Apple's test servers were the problem, not your line.

**If you want closer to 1 Gbit on the Mac, the Wi-Fi hop is the limit** — 176 Mbit at 5 GHz/−63 dBm. Ethernet would give you the other 500+.

Everything is downloaded now (APK is 590 MB and passes zip integrity), and the emulator is booting.
